recommendation_summary: The reply recommends wrapping the 03:00 cron entry in one shell line that emails the user if `nightly-sync` exits non-zero, using a mail path the sync token cannot break, and renewing the expired token.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You want to hear that nightly-sync died without reading logs. You suggested a central log on the Synology, Pieter Levels style, maybe everything in Docker. The need is an alert. The log server and Docker are a means you proposed.
labels.Deleted: A central log, the Synology, Docker, and a separate heartbeat service. You will not read logs, and those pieces do not page you when the script dies before its summary email. The crash you hit is visible as a non-zero exit, so a second monitor is extra.
labels.Bottleneck: The only alert is the summary email inside the Python job, after startup. The expired token crashed it before that email, four nights, and nothing else watches.
labels.Checked myself: You said `nightly-sync` is the only scheduled job, cron starts it at 03:00 on the Mac mini `edna`, it emails a summary when it finishes, an expired token crashed it at startup four nights with no email, and nothing else alerts. The Synology can run Docker. I have not seen the script or the crontab.

note: The reply sets up one exit-code email alert and renews the token, which fixes the cause rather than adding monitoring; it also states which failures the alert will still miss.
